title: Office — the first design, drawn in the app

steps.path: Pages button (top left) → Office, under Built in
steps.headline: Office lives with your pages, pinnable like them, and opens on a start screen with New, Recent and this project's files.
steps.changed: A built-in Office entry heads the Pages list, with its own pin. Its start screen offers a new document, spreadsheet or presentation, your recent files, and the project's other Office files.
steps.notice: Recent says when you opened each file; the project list says when each changed, and never repeats a file already under Recent.
steps.risk: Pinning Office uses one of your four pinned-page spots, as you chose.

steps.headline: On a new install the start screen says where your files will appear, and the page list shows only Office.
steps.changed: With no recent files, Recent says so in one line; Open a file… stays on its right.
steps.notice: Your own pages' welcome card is not shown here, because Office does not count as one of your pages.

steps.path: Office → a document open, with two more tabs
steps.headline: Open files become tabs; a tab left alone for a while sleeps to save memory, dimmed with a moon, and wakes where you left it.
steps.changed: YouCoded's own tab strip replaces the editor's title bar. The right end says Saved and opens Versions. Garden talk is asleep.
steps.notice: The editor below is the real one — every Word feature is there — wearing your theme's colours, font and corners.
steps.risk: The picture is the trial build of OnlyOffice 9.3 restyled; Euro-Office's editor is the same screens, and gets re-checked when we switch to it.

steps.headline: Spreadsheets and presentations get the same treatment: your theme around the editor, the sheet itself kept white.
steps.changed: Switching tabs is instant for documents that are awake; each keeps its place.
steps.notice: The grid, cells and formulas are the editor's own. Only the frame around them follows the theme.

steps.headline: Office saves as you work, and keeps earlier versions you can restore from here.
steps.changed: A Versions window lists copies kept when you opened the file and every few minutes while you worked, each with Restore.
steps.notice: Restoring keeps your current version too, so a restore can itself be undone.
steps.risk: How long versions are kept, and how many, is decided at build time; the plan is 30 days.

steps.path: A conversation → Session files → Garden plan.docx → Edit
steps.headline: Edit on a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file swaps the preview for the real editor, with a slim YouCoded toolbar and one Done.
steps.changed: One row of YouCoded buttons — undo, redo, bold, italic, underline, lists, alignment — and Open in Office. The editor's own bars are hidden.
steps.notice: There is no Save or Cancel: changes save as you make them, so Done just leaves editing. Open in Office moves the file to a full tab.
steps.risk: The quick preview you see before pressing Edit is unchanged, and PowerPoint files, which have no preview today, still show only their name until Edit.

steps.path: The practice app — Pages button, then Office
steps.headline: Try it yourself: open Office, open files from Recent, switch tabs, open Versions, then edit Garden plan.docx from a conversation's files.
steps.changed: The practice app with Office in it. The files are three sample documents; the editor is real, so typing and formatting work.
steps.notice: Nothing you do is saved, and a new blank file opens a sample of its kind.

steps.path: A conversation → Session files, with the file list open
steps.headline: Should the Edit button show while the file list is open?
steps.today: In the session files panel, the Edit button appears only once the list of files is collapsed. This already applies to text files.
steps.problem: The tester could not find any way to edit Garden plan.docx from the panel, because the list was open and Edit was hidden.

options.label: Always show Edit
pros: Editing is always one visible press away.
Works the same for text and Office files.
cons: The button floats over the document while you browse the list.

options.label: Keep it as today
pros: The document stays uncovered while you browse.
cons: New users may not find Edit at all, as the tester did not.

steps.path: Pressing Escape while a document is open
steps.headline: What should Escape do while you are working in a document?
steps.today: Everywhere else in the app, Escape closes what is in front — the Office band even says Back to chat · Esc. Inside the editor, Escape also closes its own menus.
steps.problem: Pressing Escape out of habit while typing could jump you back to chat, which may feel abrupt mid-document.

options.label: Back to chat, if idle
options.summary: Escape first closes any editor menu or dialog; with none open, it goes back to chat like everywhere else.
pros: Consistent with the rest of the app and the band's own hint.
Nothing is lost: Office saved as you went, and the tab is still there.
cons: An Escape pressed out of habit leaves the document.

options.label: Never leave Office
options.summary: Inside a document Escape only affects the editor; you leave with the band's button.
cons: The band's Esc hint would be wrong inside documents, so it would change to just Back to chat.
